analysis.title: Macro at a Glance: Latest views and forecasts (13 November 2026)
key_insights: GS now expects a third Fed hike in March 2027, after hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, to a peak policy range of 4.25-4.5%. Cuts are pushed to begin in November 2027 (previously September 2027) after the stronger-than-expected October CPI report. Terminal range is 3.25-3.5%.
GS lowered its December 2027 gold forecast to $4,650/toz from $4,800/toz because its economists now expect the third Fed hike in March 2027.
GS cut its 1Q27/2027 European natural gas (TTF) forecasts to 65/45 EUR/MWh from 74/51 EUR/MWh, citing lower supply risks.

Global real GDP is forecast at 2.8% yoy in 2027. Lower energy prices and strong AI investment growth offset tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Global core inflation is forecast to slow to 2.4% by end-2027 as the energy passthrough boost fades.

US real GDP is forecast at 2.4% Q4/Q4 in 2027, supported by the AI capex boom and lower energy prices. Core PCE is forecast to fall to 2.4% yoy by end-2027 as tariff and energy passthrough effects fade. Unemployment is forecast to end 2027 at 4.2%.

Euro area real GDP growth is forecast to slow to 0.9% Q4/Q4 in 2027 on delayed energy cost passthrough to consumers and tighter financial conditions, especially in France. Core inflation is forecast to peak at 2.9% yoy in 2Q27, helped by lingering energy passthrough and AI-related demand.
GS expects the ECB to hike 25bp once more in December to a 2.75% peak policy rate, then normalize toward a 2.25% terminal rate in 4Q27.

China real GDP is forecast at 4.5% yoy in 2027, on export strength and fading property and fiscal drags despite weak sentiment. CPI/PPI inflation is forecast to fall to 0.5%/0.3% yoy next year on lower commodity prices.
Key risks flagged are the Middle East conflict and its threat to regional energy exports, and AI capex disappointments from regulation, capacity constraints or credit market stress.

Market forecast table: S&P 500 target of 8,700 with 2027 EPS of $415 (GS) vs $426 (consensus), 2028 EPS of $460. Forecast 12m return for the S&P 500 is 14.6% and the 2027 P/E is 21.5x. US 10-year is 5.10% now, forecast 4.60% for 2027 and 4.30% for 2028. Brent is 96 now, with forecasts of 96 for 1Q27 and 90 for 2Q27.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Two more 25bp hikes (Dec 2026, Mar 2027) put the peak range at 4.25-4.5%, which implies rates stay restrictive longer.
Cuts start November 2027, two months later than the prior forecast of September 2027.
The upside surprise drove GS to add a third hike and delay cuts.

Tariff and energy passthrough effects fade.

One more 25bp hike, then normalization to a 2.25% terminal rate in 4Q27.
Export strength and fading property and fiscal drags.

risk_factors: Middle East conflict and risks to regional energy exports.
AI capex disappointments owing to regulation, capacity constraints, or credit market stress, which could weigh on economies and markets.
Tighter financial conditions, especially in France.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict remains fluid, with risks to the region's energy exports.
